rule_summary: NEM threshold (CGS Net Metered rate) is <300 kW aggregate nameplate, well above the 20 kW PSC 119 statewide default. rule_summary: Net Metering (Pg-2) applies to systems <=100 kW (state default is 20 kW — MGE is well above); Parallel Generation (Pg-1) rate applies above 100 kW. For net metering customers, exported energy credited at same retail rate as imported energy (1:1) for the first 12 months. Beginning month 13, if the customer has been a net exporter over the trailing 12 months ('Net Seller'), excess credits roll over at the lower Parallel Generation Buyback Rate instead of retail rate — a significant behind-the-scenes de-rate for oversized systems not paired with storage. MGE guidance explicitly warns customers not to oversize solar without adding a battery, given this Net Seller de-rate.
export_credit_value: Year 1: retail rate (1:1); Year 13+ for Net Sellers: Parallel Generation Buyback Rate (lower than retail, exact cents/kWh not confirmed in sources reviewed)

rule_summary: DEMEC is a joint-action wholesale power agency representing 9 Delaware municipal electric departments (New Castle, Newark, Middletown, Smyrna, Clayton, Dover, Milford, Seaford, Lewes); each member municipality sets its OWN net-metering/interconnection tariff and is exempt from PSC rules per 26 Del. Following SB 298 (2022): excess kWh credits revert to the utility (no payout, no rollover) at the end of each member's annualized billing period; DEMEC's recommended (and most members') practice is an annualized period running spring-to-spring so summer-generated credits carry through winter consumption (contrast with DE Electric Coop's rockier transition, and with Delmarva which lets customers choose their own true-up month). Non-residential net-metering customers pay the full reasonable cost of any new/replacement net meter; residential customers pay up to $200 -- statewide statutory floor, but METER COST is billed directly to the customer at DEMEC members (verify this is not absorbed by any individual member as a local incentive). Utilities may consider system reliability/safety/capacity when reviewing interconnection and net-metering applications (SB 298), giving DEMEC members discretion PSC-regulated Delmarva may have less of.

storage_specific_notes: Each of the 9 member municipalities (Newark, Milford, Seaford, Smyrna, Dover, Lewes, Middletown, Clayton, New Castle) may have its own interconnection agreement text and minor local variations -- treat this row as the DEMEC-coordinated baseline, not a guarantee that every member is identical; confirm against the specific municipality's own utility department before finalizing a project in that territory.

Potomac Edison also uniquely still applies community-solar credits as a kWh USAGE REDUCTION on subscriber bills rather than a dollar credit (per PSC's Nov 2025 net metering report) -- transitions to dollar-credit method 1/1/2026, a live utility-specific billing-mechanics change relevant to any MD savings modeling tool.

rule_summary: SMECO is a cooperative but, unlike Delaware's DEC, MD's COMAR 20.50 net metering/interconnection rules are written to bind 'electric companies' inclusive of cooperatives -- SMECO's PSC Net Metering Report data (avg. April 2025 credit $58.08 across 3,612 residential accounts) is reported alongside the IOUs under the same statewide cap/sizing framework, with no distinct SMECO-specific cap or sizing deviation identified. NOT independently confirmed among the four utilities that filed 2020 PSC storage pilot proposals (BGE, Pepco, Delmarva, Potomac Edison) -- SMECO does not appear to have participated in the utility-owned storage pilot program, which may mean SMECO territory has less utility-side storage infrastructure/experience than the four Exelon/FirstEnergy utilities, though this is an inference, not a confirmed absence.
storage_specific_notes: No SMECO-specific storage tariff or BYOD program identified in sources reviewed this pass -- if SMECO customers want compensated storage participation, the DRIVE Act EDSSS pilots (BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison) do NOT appear to include SMECO; verify directly with SMECO before assuming parity.

rule_summary: Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 net metering caps/sizing. Choptank publishes its own supplemental interconnection capacity guidance: individual interconnections are restricted to no larger than 3 MVA on 12kV circuits and 5 MVA on 25kV circuits -- a circuit-voltage-class-based ceiling ABOVE the state's 2MW net-metering cap itself, relevant mainly to larger C&I/grid-supply projects seeking non-net-metered interconnection or exceeding net-metering-eligible size. Choptank markets aggregation, solar, net metering, AND energy storage together on a single program page, suggesting more explicit co-op-level support/guidance for storage-paired systems than some peers.
storage_specific_notes: Choptank's marketing groups 'Solar, Net Metering, Aggregation & Energy Storage' together -- suggests an established storage-interconnection pathway, but specific grid-charging/non-export terms not independently retrieved this pass (page required JavaScript, could not fetch full text).

rule_summary: Municipal utility; follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps/sizing but reports its own local net-metered solar capacity: 3.49 MW installed as of 6/30/2025 (per PSC Net Metering Report). No charge to install a net meter at Easton (a favorable deviation vs. utilities that pass through meter costs). Easton allows aggregate NEM combining a single host account with child accounts under the statewide aggregation rules for agricultural/municipal/nonprofit entities.

Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps. Delmarva's PSC storage pilot is notably different in character from BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison's substation-scale utility-owned BESS: Delmarva contracted with Sunverge Energy to deploy BEHIND-THE-METER residential battery systems in 110 homes in Elk Neck, networked together to function as a virtual power plant (aggregated 0.5 MW / 1.5 MWh). This IS the closest match in the MD pilot program to a customer-sited/BYOD-style storage model referenced in the research brief -- distinguish from BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison's utility-owned substation/grid-asset pilots, which are NOT customer-owned-device programs.
storage_specific_notes: Elk Neck VPP (Sunverge, 110 homes, 0.5MW/1.5MWh aggregated) is the pilot most resembling a BYOD/customer-storage model in MD; confirm current operational status and whether it has a successor commercial program before assuming it's still active as of 2026.

utility_name: Virginia Electric & Power Co (Dominion Energy Virginia)
rule_summary: Dominion's residential/small-C&I tariff sub-caps nonresidential systems at 1 MW (below the 3 MW statewide statutory ceiling). Following the SCC's April 30, 2026 final order (Case No. PUR-2025-00079), Dominion is rolling out a 'NEM 2.0' tariff for customers who interconnect after the order's effective date: 1:1 kWh crediting and 12-month (annual) netting are preserved, but the year-end net-excess-generation cash-out rate rises to $0.05829/kWh (includes a new $0.01/kWh credit for avoided RPS/REC compliance cost) and a $1/month administrative fee applies. The SCC rejected Dominion's proposed $100-750 application fee and its proposed 30-minute netting/dollar-based interval crediting. Pre-order NEM 1.0 customers remain grandfathered indefinitely and may switch to NEM 2.0 only if it becomes more favorable to them. Low-income customers may choose whichever tariff (legacy or NEM 2.0) is more favorable. Separately, the SCC-authorized standby charge threshold rises from 15 kW AC to 20 kW AC effective 7/1/2026 under HB 1255.
nem_aggregate_cap: 6% of prior-year peak load statewide; Dominion-specific current subscription level not published in sources reviewed
export_credit_value: Legacy (NEM 1.0): year-end excess at avoided cost (~3.5c/kWh, last published 2019 figure); NEM 2.0 (new interconnections after ~mid-2026): $0.05829/kWh year-end excess cash-out, effective per April 30, 2026 SCC order
ic_application_fee: $0 application fee (SCC rejected Dominion's proposed $100-750 fee); $1/month administrative fee applies to NEM 2.0 customers only
ic_study_trigger_kw: Not published as a distinct kW threshold beyond standard Level 1/2/3 SGF review tiers
external_disconnect: Required per Dominion Terms and Conditions Section XXV for net-metered generating facilities
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-but-not-credited (grid-charged battery discharge is not distinguished from PV export in metering; Off-Peak Plan customers have export credited at the on/off/super-off-peak rate of the interval generated)
standby_charge: $2.79/kW distribution + $1.40/kW transmission standby charge per month on Schedules 1/1G (approx.); $4.19/kW distribution + $1.32/kW transmission on Schedule 1S; charge is based on the customer's peak monthly kW pulled from the grid, not on generation
standby_threshold_kw: 20 kW AC effective 7/1/2026 (raised from 15 kW AC under HB 1255; was 10 kW AC 2011-earlier revision)
storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to an existing net-metered system does not by itself void grandfathering under the April 2026 SCC order language ('nothing...shall affect any eligible customer-generator...who interconnect before the effective date'), but any change in interconnected AC nameplate capacity requires a new interconnection application per company practice, and if the resulting aggregate AC capacity crosses the 15/20 kW standby-charge threshold it will newly trigger the standby charge — this specific battery-retrofit scenario is not explicitly addressed in Dominion's public net metering materials and should be confirmed directly with the company (flagged in gaps file). AC-coupled vs DC-coupled battery treatment and metering configuration requirements are not detailed in sources reviewed.

Full retail 1:1 credit for self-consumed solar within the 12-month banking period is preserved. Net excess generation (true excess beyond annual consumption) is now compensated at a rate that includes REC value and exceeds the prior default PJM LMP-based avoided-cost rate. The 6% aggregate cap was retained (APCo had sought a reduction).

Customers who apply after that date are subject to a fixed export credit of approximately 12.4 cents/kWh (67-75% of full retail rate, roughly a 27% cut from the effective 1:1 value) instead of 1:1 crediting. The PSC granted APCo/Wheeling Power customers a full extra year of grandfathering runway beyond what the company originally requested.

utility_name: Consolidated Edison Co of New York (Con Edison)
rule_summary: Follows the statewide SIR for process and timelines, but its territory is dominated by underground secondary-network and spot-network grid, which changes what interconnection actually costs. Con Edison publishes CESIR cost ranges of up to about $20,000 for inverter-based systems and about $27,000 for rotating machines. On spot/isolated networks the default is a reverse-power relay that prevents export; since 2012 Con Edison offers Communications Aided Tripping (CAT) - insensitive network-protector settings plus SCADA, anti-islanding and DNP3 telemetry - to allow export on network service, at a project cost on the order of $100,000. Con Edison states it is the only utility in the nation allowing export on network service. Interconnection portal split at 50 kW-AC (Small DG vs Large DG); for hybrid projects the portal is chosen by export capability rather than combined nameplate. 2026 Customer Benefit Contribution: net-metered PV $1.29/kW-mo residential and $1.47/kW-mo small commercial; Value Stack PV $0.65 and $1.03.
ic_study_trigger_kw: In underground secondary network areas a CESIR may be required even for systems at or below 50 kW (SIR Sec I.C Exception 1); Con Edison-published CESIR cost up to ~$20,000 inverter-based and ~$27,000 rotating machine.
non_export_option: Yes - reverse power relay preventing export is Con Edison's traditional approach on spot and isolated networks; CAT is the paid alternative that permits export.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes - see state row. Con Edison requires charging kW (peak kW/kVA needed to charge) to be stated in the application scope of work; if it exceeds the local service, service upgrades may be required.
standby_charge: Standby Service under General Rule 20, plus the Rider Q Standby Pilot Rate Program (customer-selected contract demand and As-Used demand period) and SC-11 Buy-Back Service (LBMP, grossed up by 1.066 for secondary-level deliveries). Published standby rates (as of retrieval): residential contract demand $6.05/kW plus $20 customer charge; small business $8.77/kW plus $33; large commercial low-tension under 1,500 kW $9.18/kW plus $71.
standby_threshold_kw: 50 - customers with Contract Demand below 50 kW are reported exempt from mandatory Standby Service billing under General Rule 20.3, as are customers whose on-site generation nameplate is no more than 15% of maximum potential demand served from all sources. This aligns the standby threshold with the SIR's 50 kW expedited/large-project boundary. Threshold is SECONDARY-sourced - not read in the General Rule 20 tariff leaf.
storage_specific_notes: Con Edison states that SC1 residential customers under 25 kW-AC and SC2 small commercial customers under 2 MW-AC who install an ESS after 2017-03-10 receive Phase One NEM compensation, and that residential and small commercial customers are eligible to pair grid-parallel storage with solar and take service under Phase One NEM - i.e. adding a battery does not by itself force a move off Phase One NEM. Storage may only be added to a Phase One NEM system if it is paired with another Phase One NEM-eligible technology. Adding an ESS to an existing DG facility is filed as a Battery Energy Storage application with SIR Appendix K; a new PV plus new storage project is filed as a single Hybrid application. Metering: three acceptable hybrid configurations - exclusive ESS charge from PV, PV export only, and separate metering; the PSC approved a three-meter configuration for hybrid ESS in Case 18-E-0081, Order Modifying Standardized Interconnection Requirements issued 2018-04-19. Technologies behind one meter that are credited under different rate structures require specialized metering and/or relaying. NOTE: this guide is Version 4, July 2022, aligned to the May 2022 SIR - re-verify against the 2026-02-09 SIR.

NEM2/NEM-ST legacy provisions, 'Pursuant to D.22-12-056'): the addition of energy storage to the existing Generating Facility shall not disqualify the customer from the remainder of the 20-year Transition Period. utility_name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
rule_summary: Municipal utility outside CPUC jurisdiction; not bound by Rule 21 or the NBT. Governed by the LADWP NEM Service Rider and NEM Guidelines (rev. 11/23/2020, amended Jan 2021) plus the LADWP Electric Service Requirements (ESR). Export credit is still retail-rate kWh netting (credit applied to later bills except taxes and minimum charges; any credit balance is zeroed with no payout when service terminates). NEM eligible rates: R-1, A-1, A-2, A-3. Systems >1 MW-AC(CEC) go to Parallel Generation Schedule CG-2 or CG-3. Process: online application at the Solar Automated Meter Spot portal for a Work Request number; PV <10 kW-AC without service upgrade or battery backup may be fast-tracked; inspections by LADBS, LADWP Electric Service Representative (>=10 kW and some smaller cases) and LADWP Solar Inspector. Interconnection Agreement required where PV and/or ESS >10 kW-AC: Short-Form IA for >10 to <=30 kW-AC, Long-Form IA with single-line diagram for PV >30 kW-AC. All grid-interconnected Energy Storage Systems require preliminary review and inspection by an LADWP Distribution Engineer and ESR (so storage never gets the PV fast track).
nem_cap_res_kw: 1000 kW-AC (CEC) for NEM; larger systems go to Schedule CG-2/CG-3
export_credit_value: Retail-rate netting (confirmed; values captured elsewhere)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 30 kW-AC - Long-Form IA and Distribution Engineer review above this; any ESS triggers Distribution Engineer/ESR review
external_disconnect: Required - all PV systems must have a disconnect device per the LADWP ESR, readily accessible and located near the billing/performance meter
non_export_option: Yes - ESR requires power controls to prevent inadvertent export where required, with settings adjustable only by the manufacturer or its designated qualified worker, not the customer (Secondary - ESR Sec. 8i as indexed, PDF not rendered)
storage_specific_notes: Per LADWP ESR Sec. 8i (as indexed by search; PDF would not render for direct reading): battery storage may not export to the grid under NEM unless it is exclusively charged by eligible renewable parallel generation - so a grid-charged battery must be controlled as non-export. Battery retrofit: LADWP NEM is still open retail-rate netting with no legacy/successor split, so adding a battery does not change export compensation; the retrofit does require a Distribution Engineer/ESR review and, if the ESS is >10 kW-AC, an Interconnection Agreement. Battery-backup projects are excluded from the <10 kW solar fast track.

rule_summary: Publicly-owned utility outside CPUC jurisdiction (SMUD Board sets rates). Interconnection under SMUD's own Rule and Regulation 21 and Rate Policy 11-01 Interconnection Guidelines (Feb 2022); interconnected energy storage is treated as distributed generation under Rule 21. Applications via PowerClerk; SMUD may require agreements up to 500 kW and generally requires executed agreements above 500 kW; small-generator distribution process typically <=20 MW. Uses Rule 21 or SMUD Advanced Inverter Function (AIF) settings. Export regime: Rate Schedule SSR (Solar and Storage Rate) mandatory for renewable generation approved on or after 2022-03-01 - residential must be on R-TOD; sized to offset up to 110% of own requirements; max 3,000 kW; all kWh registered on the bi-directional meter as delivered to SMUD credited at the Export Compensation Rate ($0.0960/kWh eff. 2026-06-01, updated every 4 years, max +/-30%); credit offsets only usage charges and carries forward. Legacy NEM1 customers (approved before 2022-03-01) may stay on NEM1 through 2030-12-31.
export_credit_value: SSR $0.0960/kWh flat export rate eff. 2026-06-01 (confirmed; captured elsewhere)
ic_application_fee: Rule 21 Interconnection Fee (Rate Policy 9-02, eff. 2026-06-01, non-refundable, applies to new solar and battery storage incl. storage-only): residential <10 kW $500; residential >=10 to <20 kW $1,000; commercial (and residential >=20 kW) <100 kW $2,500; >=100 to <500 kW $3,350; >=500 kW $5,000 plus cost-based invoice for remaining work incl. telemetry. Prior values $180/$300/$2,000/$2,400. NEM1 customers adding storage are not charged the fee (SMUD FAQ, Secondary).
ic_study_trigger_kw: 500 - executed interconnection agreements generally required above 500 kW; >=500 kW also triggers cost-based billing for remaining interconnection work
non_export_option: Yes - dedicated Non-export interconnection request path in PowerClerk for battery, EV and other DERs not intended to export to the distribution system
standby_threshold_kw: N/A - SSR customers are exempt from generator standby charges on load served by the eligible facility (SSR Sec. III)
storage_specific_notes: Grid charging: SMUD's interconnection page states that to qualify for NEM (NEM1) all storage must be charged with renewable energy on site. Under SSR the tariff defines export as all kWh registered on the bi-directional meter as delivered to SMUD and lets storage-only facilities take SSR, so grid-charged export appears to be credited at the flat SSR rate - this is a reading of the tariff text, not an explicit SMUD statement (flat rate makes arbitrage value low anyway). Battery retrofit on legacy NEM1: SMUD says existing NEM customers can add a battery and stay on NEM1 through 2030-12-31 but are then NOT eligible for My Energy Optimizer Partner+ storage incentives; any customer receiving a SMUD storage incentive must be on SSR (SSR Sec. VIII). Expanding generation by more than the greater of 10% or 1 kW (or beyond 110% of original) forces a move to SSR and a new application. Conflict: the same SMUD FAQ also says customers on NEM who add battery storage will be placed on SSR - read as the incentive path. Storage-only customers cannot be on NEM1. Sizing: SMUD materials (Secondary) allow SSR PV up to 120% of 12-month usage when storage is added; tariff text says 110%.

rule_summary: Irrigation district (publicly owned) outside CPUC jurisdiction; sets its own rules. NEM closed: IID set its PU Code 2827 NEM obligation at 50.2 MW (5% of 1,004 MW 2010 peak) and reached it in early 2016. Since July 2016 all new interconnections go on the Net Billing Program (Distributive Self-Generation Service rate schedule): instantaneous netting - load is billed at the regular rate and generation exceeding instantaneous load is paid at IID's lowest wholesale solar contract cost (6.98 c/kWh as posted; variable, adjusted by the district). No participation cap on Net Billing. Interconnection agreement for Net Billing covers renewable facilities of 1 MW or less. Applications only via PowerClerk (since 2024-01-01). Two document tiers: AC nameplate <10 kW (checklist, AC disconnect cut sheet, inverter manual, bi-directional meter fee) and >=10 kW and microgrids (adds IID Rule 21 application). Solar inspection fee $255 per application received after 2025-05-01; Customer Service Proposal fees changed 2025-03-01.
nem_cap_res_kw: 1000 kW (Net Billing interconnection agreement covers facilities of 1 MW or less)
nem_aggregate_cap: NEM: 50.2 MW (5% of 2010 peak of 1,004 MW) - reached early 2016, closed. Net Billing: no cap.
aggregate_cap_status: NEM fully subscribed and closed; NEM 4,212 interconnections / 63.62 MW; Net Billing 880 interconnections / 12.48 MW (IID PU Code 2827(c)(3)(A) report, date not stated on page)
export_credit_value: Net Billing export at 6.98 c/kWh (variable; confirmed, captured elsewhere)
ic_application_fee: $255 solar inspection fee per application (after 2025-05-01) plus bi-directional meter cost where the existing meter cannot measure two-way flow; other CSP charges may apply
ic_study_trigger_kw: 10 - IID Rule 21 application required at AC nameplate >=10 kW and for microgrids
external_disconnect: Required - an AC disconnect cut sheet is a required application document at every size tier
storage_specific_notes: No IID storage-specific rule found on the IID interconnection, NEM or Net Billing pages (only a 'microgrids' application tier). Grid charging treatment, storage metering configuration, and whether adding a battery to a legacy NEM system moves the customer to Net Billing are all Unclear - IID directs questions to its Distributed Interconnection Unit (solar@iid.com). Net Billing uses instantaneous netting, so any storage discharge that exceeds instantaneous load is paid only at the ~7 c/kWh wholesale solar rate.

rule_summary: Irrigation district (publicly owned) outside CPUC jurisdiction; own Electric Service Rule No. 21 and Solar Electric Service Guide. Only NEM 2.0 is offered to new customers: real-time (hourly for residential) netting - imports at MID retail rate, generation exceeding load at that time credited at 7.6 c/kWh as a bill credit. Sizing: PV may not exceed 115% of the meter's annual demonstrated load (CSI calculator); modifications also capped at 115%. Above 1 MW customers pay a capacity charge per kW over the threshold and forfeit excess-generation credits. Application package: MID Solar System & Energy Storage Device Application, Electrical Interconnection Agreement, Net Metering Agreement, single-line diagram, battery data sheet if a battery is installed. MID review up to 30 days; interconnection inspection up to 10 business days; PV+ESS sites need an inspection appointment. MID installs a utility-grade production meter on the AC side of the inverter (customer supplies socket). NEM 1.0 customers who add or rearrange panels increasing output by more than 10% must move to NEM 2.0; NEM 2.0 customers must wait 6 months after interconnection before modifying panels.
nem_cap_res_kw: No kW cap stated; 115% of annual demonstrated load; above 1 MW capacity charge applies and excess credits are forfeited
export_credit_value: NEM 2.0 excess generation 7.6 c/kWh (confirmed; captured elsewhere)
ic_application_fee: $900 per meter for systems <100 kW AC (CSI rating); $1,800 per meter for >=100 kW AC
ic_study_trigger_kw: 1000 - capacity charge per kW above 1 MW and loss of excess generation credits
external_disconnect: Required - two visible, lockable AC disconnect switches between the PV system and MID's system (one between the panel and production meter socket, within 12 ft and line of sight of the main panel), per MID Solar Electric Service Guide (2019)
non_export_option: Yes - effectively mandatory for storage: MID's Service Guide says all ESS shall be configured for customer backup power or peak shaving only and shall not export to MID's system; a Smart Contactor may be used to disconnect the ESS on voltage/frequency abnormality
storage_specific_notes: Storage must be non-exporting (backup or peak shaving only) per MID Solar Electric Service Guide, Solar PV With Optional Energy Storage Systems, June 1 2019 (read from MID's azurewebsites dev mirror - re-verify against the current mid.org version). The guide shows five approved DG-with-battery interconnection configurations (Drawings PV-012.0 to PV-016.0). Since storage cannot export, a grid-charged battery earns no export credit; charging source is not otherwise restricted in the text read. Battery retrofit: the NEM 1.0 to NEM 2.0 trigger stated by MID is adding or rearranging panels that raise output by more than 10%; whether adding only a battery forces a NEM 1.0 customer onto NEM 2.0 is Unclear (not addressed on the pages read). Customers modifying an existing PV system must submit new Interconnection and Net Metering Agreements.

rule_summary: Irrigation district (publicly owned) outside CPUC jurisdiction. Retail net metering (Schedules RNT residential and NNT non-residential) is closed to new accounts (Secondary: closed at the start of 2015). New solar customers move to a Self-Generation rate schedule (DG domestic, CG commercial, FG farm, IG small industrial, HG large industrial, BG bulk industrial, MG municipal, SG) with Customer, Demand and TOU Energy charges. Netting is within each on-peak and off-peak period over the month; any monthly excess is credited at TID's Short Run Marginal Cost (published daily). No aggregation. System size not limited to load under the self-generation schedules, but TID reserves the right to require an interconnection study or limit size. Interconnection: Application for Interconnection, wiring diagram, inverter/panel spec sheets and CSI calculator report; TID field inspection before metering; TID Solar Installation Guidelines (2025) govern construction (one dedicated PV breaker per MSP, 120% bus rule, no line-side taps on residential). Adding generation to an existing solar service requires a new single-line diagram for approval.
nem_cap_res_kw: No load-based cap under self-generation schedules; TID may limit size or require study
aggregate_cap_status: RNT/NNT net metering closed to new accounts
export_credit_value: Excess monthly TOU-period generation credited at TID Short Run Marginal Cost (published daily; confirmed, captured elsewhere)
ic_application_fee: $450 residential; $775 non-residential under 1 MW (effective 2025-01-01); first inspection free, $150 per re-inspection trip; optional generation meter typically $600; >1 MW contact TID
ic_study_trigger_kw: 1000 - projects over 1 MW handled case by case; TID may require an interconnection study at any size
external_disconnect: Not required by default - AC disconnect only 'if installed'; required for line-side taps and when the optional TID generation meter is used
storage_specific_notes: TID Solar Installation Guidelines (2025) Sec. 6: battery storage must be operable at TID inspection with a contractor representative present; it must be demonstrated that the system cannot back-feed when TID power is interrupted (anti-islanding, not an export ban); battery kWh and kW must be on the single-line diagram. No TID rule found on grid charging, on whether battery discharge exports are credited at SRMC, or on whether adding a battery to a legacy RNT/NNT net-metering account forfeits it - all Unclear. Note: legacy RNT/NNT schedules are only posted as issuu embeds (not read).

rule_summary: City-owned utility outside CPUC jurisdiction. Distributed generation (including microgrids) interconnects under Rule 22 of Anaheim's Rules, Rates and Regulations plus Anaheim's Generation Interconnection Standards and Guidelines and a Standard Form Interconnection Agreement (Rule 21 does not apply). Retail kWh-for-kWh NEM was offered up to 5% (30 MW) of peak aggregate load; that cap was met in 2019. Solar billing accounts set up after 2021-01-01 take NEM 2.0 (Developmental Schedule D-NEM): wholesale-based export credit - an hourly TOU 'ACC' (Annual Cash Compensation) rate paid for all energy sent back to the grid from a solar PV system each bill cycle. Anaheim states it is not moving to a CPUC-style NEM 3.0. Interconnection studies required for large systems (>1 MW) per Secondary search summary of a Jan 2026 Public Utilities Board rule-modification item (not read).
nem_aggregate_cap: Legacy retail NEM: 5% of peak aggregate load (30 MW)
aggregate_cap_status: Legacy retail NEM cap reached in 2019 - closed
export_credit_value: NEM 2.0 hourly ACC export rates (e.g. summer weekday 5-9 pm $0.0938/kWh; off-peak $0.0375/kWh), updated annually, current table expires 2026-06-30 (confirmed; captured elsewhere)
storage_specific_notes: Anaheim frames NEM 2.0 as designed to reward storage (store daytime excess rather than export at wholesale credit). Its residential battery rebate (up to $3,000) requires a UL-certified system of at least 5 kWh, standalone or paired with existing PV, a TOU rate and 12 months in the MyPower Savings program. The ACC export rate is defined as paid for energy sent back to the grid 'from a solar photovoltaic system', which implies grid-charged battery exports are not the credited quantity, but no explicit grid-charging or metering rule was found - Unclear. Whether adding a battery to a pre-2021 legacy retail-NEM account moves it to NEM 2.0 was not found - Unclear. Rule 22, the Generation Interconnection Standards and Schedule D-NEM PDFs did not render for reading.

rule_summary: City-owned utility outside CPUC jurisdiction. Interconnection under RPU Electric Rule 22 'Distributed Generation Facilities Interconnection' (eff. 2022-05-10), a Rule 21-style process with Initial and Supplemental Review, non-export designation and certification/testing provisions. Export regime: Schedule SELF-GEN (eff. 2022-11-01; Board Res. 2022-1, Council Res. 23852) for renewable facilities up to 5,000 kW: all imports billed at the otherwise-applicable tariff (residential single-family assigned D-TOU); each kWh supplied to the grid is credited at the Avoided Cost of Energy (ACOE) - CAISO day-ahead LMP at the Vista take-out point plus capacity, ancillary, transmission, GHG, RPS and loss components, 3-year historical average, reset each July 1 - applied by TOU period; credits roll forward and any balance is PAID at termination of service. Sizing: up to 150% of annual consumption (more with proof of added load); maximum export to RPU's system 1,000 kW. Program cap 64 MW including existing Schedule NEM customers. Customers on an existing NEM agreement are not affected.
nem_cap_res_kw: Facility <=5,000 kW; sized <=150% of annual consumption; export limited to 1,000 kW
nem_aggregate_cap: 64 MW program cap (SELF-GEN plus legacy NEM customers)
export_credit_value: ACOE avoided-cost export credit by TOU period, reset each July 1 (confirmed; captured elsewhere)
ic_application_fee: Rule 22 Initial Review fee: NEM residential $225; commercial flat and demand $360; commercial TOU $865; all others $800 plus $600 Supplemental Review; 50% of the Initial Review fee refunded if rejected or withdrawn
non_export_option: Yes - Rule 22 defines Non-Exporting facilities and provides a certified Non-Export designation and Non-Export test procedure (relays or other export-limiting functions), modeled on CA Rule 21 Sec. J.3.e
storage_specific_notes: Neither Schedule SELF-GEN nor Rule 22 (full text searched) contains the word 'storage'. SELF-GEN credits kWh 'supplied by their Renewable Electrical Generating Facility' and counts 'additions or enhancements' to a renewable facility as part of it, which suggests - but does not state - that renewable-paired storage exports are creditable and grid-charged exports are not. Grid-charging treatment and metering configuration for paired storage: Unclear. Battery retrofit on a legacy RPU NEM agreement: RPU says existing NEM agreements are not affected by SELF-GEN, but no rule found on whether adding a battery changes that - Unclear. RPU runs a separate Energy Storage Rebate Program (not reviewed for interconnection terms).

utility_name: Silicon Valley Power (City of Santa Clara)
rule_summary: City-owned utility outside CPUC jurisdiction. Still offers full retail net energy metering under Rate Schedule NM (eff. 2026-01-01, Res. 25-9516): renewable (solar/wind/hybrid) facilities up to 1 MW, energy billed on a net basis with an annual bill per PU Code 2827 (demand-metered customers pay monthly with annual true-up); annual excess is either paid at the Payment Rate for Excess Energy ($0.05366/kWh for 2026 = avoided gas-fired energy cost + unbundled REC value) or carried to the next annual cycle at the customer's option. Load aggregation option for contiguous properties (forfeits net surplus compensation). Available first-come first-served until total capacity reaches 5.0% of SVP annual peak distribution demand; SVP says a successor tariff (possibly priced differently from CPUC NEM 2.0/3.0) will follow once the 5% threshold is exceeded - timing not set. Interconnection: SVP interconnection agreement plus SD 1630 Initial Review Process and SD 1631 Engineering & Operating Requirements, SVP-DP-001 protection requirements; applications via PowerClerk; PV and ESS need SVP pre-approval before applying for building permits, and PTO before energizing. Standby service not required for NM customers.
nem_aggregate_cap: 5.0% of SVP annual peak distribution demand
aggregate_cap_status: Not published on pages read; SVP says a successor will be set when the 5% threshold is exceeded - watch item
export_credit_value: Full retail netting; annual excess $0.05366/kWh (2026) (confirmed; captured elsewhere)
standby_charge: None for NM customers - Schedule NM says service under a standby rate schedule shall not be required
storage_specific_notes: Schedule NM definition: if the renewable facility is used with energy storage, the storage inverter must not (1) be larger than the Renewable Generating Facility or (2) discharge for more than four hours - i.e. storage is allowed on NEM but capped at PV inverter size and 4-hour duration. No rule found on grid charging or on whether storage discharge exports are netted at retail - Unclear. Battery retrofit: Schedule NM is still open (no legacy/successor split yet), so adding a compliant battery does not by itself change export compensation; a successor tariff is pending the 5% trigger. SD 1630/1631 and SVP-DP-001 were not read.

rule_summary: City-owned utility outside CPUC jurisdiction. GWP still offers NEM (no incentives): excess generation is a bill credit applied automatically when needed; GWP publishes a calendar-year NEM Compensation Rate for surplus (2025: $0.05639/kWh; 2024 $0.0762; 2023 $0.0817). Sizing: 110% of historical usage cap, except residential and commercial PV up to 10 kW CEC-AC are exempt with self-certification (since 2023-11-01). Applications via PowerClerk; only the Interconnection Agreement dated 2026-01-01 accepted from 2026-01-19. Two process guides: residential <15 kW CEC-AC, and commercial plus residential >=15 kW CEC-AC. Technical requirements in GWP Electrical Service Requirements - Distributed Energy Resources Specifications (DERS). Inverters with Power Control Systems (PCS) allowed since 2023-11-01 with a Power Control System Agreement.
nem_cap_res_kw: 110% of historical usage (PV <=10 kW CEC-AC exempt)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 110% of historical usage (PV <=10 kW CEC-AC exempt)
export_credit_value: NEM surplus compensation rate 2025 $0.05639/kWh (confirmed; captured elsewhere)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 15 kW CEC-AC - residential systems at or above this follow the commercial application guide
external_disconnect: Utility discretion - an AC disconnect is shown with the ES meter location in GWP's energy storage guide and DERS diagrams; details in DERS (not read)
non_export_option: Yes - PCS-capable inverters allowed with a Power Control System Agreement (since 2023-11-01)
storage_specific_notes: Storage: customers qualifying for the <=10 kW PV exemption may install up to 30 kWh of PV-paired energy storage; a separate energy storage meter is no longer required for any residential or commercial ESS (since 2023-11-01) - note GWP's separate Energy Storage application page still describes an ES meter and Spot drawing process, so that page appears out of date. ESS applications go through PowerClerk, GWP Engineering review against DERS, city permit, B&S and GWP inspections. No GWP rule found on grid charging or on whether storage exports are netted - Unclear. Battery retrofit: GWP NEM is still open with no legacy/successor split, so adding a battery does not by itself change export compensation (no rule found saying otherwise).

rule_summary: Follows NC state row (it is built from the DEC/DEP compliance tariffs). DEC-specific values: Rider NMB (Leaf 143) and Rider RSC (Leaf 141, requires R-TOU-CPP) NEEC 3.35 c/kWh; NBC $0.28/kW-month on nameplate (kW DC solar); RSC grid access fee $2.05/kW above 15 kW; minimum bill $22 (customer+distribution portion) on both; NMB annual caps 14,500/31,900/35,100/38,700 kW AC for 2023-2026, closed 1/1/2027. Legacy Rider NM (Leaf 72) residential participants must move to NMB or another rider by 1/1/2027. PowerPair battery incentive requires NMB or RSC.
nem_aggregate_cap: Rider NMB annual enrollment caps (kW AC): 2023 14,500; 2024 31,900; 2025 35,100; 2026 38,700
aggregate_cap_status: Not verified (no public NMB subscription report found)
export_credit_value: 3.35 c/kWh NEEC (NMB and RSC, compliance tariff eff. July 2023; later updates not checked)
grid_charging_allowed: No - NMB/RSC/NM admit only storage 'configured to receive electrical charge solely from onsite renewable energy generation'
standby_charge: NBC $0.28/kW-mo; RSC Grid Access Fee $2.05/kW-mo above 15 kW; $22 minimum bill
storage_specific_notes: Battery must charge solely from onsite renewables to stay on NM/NMB/RSC. Battery retrofit: customer must notify Nameplate Capacity change in writing within 60 days; Bridge Rate Period is 15 yrs from 'submission date of the applicable interconnection application' - whether a battery interconnection application restarts or preserves the term, or forces RSC, is not stated (Unclear). Legacy NM ends 12/31/2026 for all residential anyway. NCIP 1.5.2 treats added DC-side storage as not a Material Modification when output profile is unchanged. Nameplate for NBC/GAF is kW DC for solar or kW AC for non-solar - battery kW treatment not stated.

rule_summary: Follows NC state row. DEP-specific values: Rider NMB-1 and RSC-2 NEEC 3.40 c/kWh; NBC $0.62/kW-month; RSC grid access fee $1.50/kW above 15 kW; minimum bill $22 (NMB) / $28 (RSC, requires R-TOU-CPP); LIEAP/CIP recipients with <=8 kW DC exempt from NMB minimum bill; NMB annual caps 16,350/35,900/39,500/43,500 kW AC for 2023-2026, closed 1/1/2027. Legacy Rider NM-5 (lesser of max annual demand or 1,000 kW; standby waived for residential and GS <=100 kW) closed to new residential; transfer by 1/1/2027. DEP PowerPair reported at capacity mid-2026 (program chunk).
nem_aggregate_cap: Rider NMB annual enrollment caps (kW AC): 2023 16,350; 2024 35,900; 2025 39,500; 2026 43,500
export_credit_value: 3.40 c/kWh NEEC (NMB-1 and RSC-2, compliance tariff eff. July 2023; later updates not checked)
grid_charging_allowed: No - NMB-1/RSC-2 admit only storage 'configured to receive electrical charge solely from onsite renewable energy generation'
standby_charge: NBC $0.62/kW-mo; RSC Grid Access Fee $1.50/kW-mo above 15 kW; minimum bill $22 (NMB) / $28 (RSC)
storage_specific_notes: Same storage rules as DEC: renewable-only charging; 60-day written notice of Nameplate Capacity changes; no rider language on whether a battery addition restarts the 15-yr NMB term or forces RSC (Unclear).

rule_summary: Follows SC state row (Act 62). DEC SC: Rider RSC (Leaf 136, requires R-STOU; per-TOU-period netting, CPP exports netted against On-Peak; net excess $0.0397/kWh; NBC on nameplate; minimum bill = Basic Facilities Charge + rate minimum). New Rider NMT (Leaf 138, Order 2025-453, eff. 1/1/2026) for legacy RNM/IRSC customers: any residential rate, monthly netting with excess at 4.19 c/kWh, NMT for up to 10 yrs from NMT Start Date (1/1/2026 for pre-5/16/2019 applications, ending 12/31/2035; 6/1/2029 for later applications, ending 5/31/2039), then Rider RSC; enrollment window 6 months before to 12 months after NMT Start. NMT NBC: base $0.00/kW; rider NBC $0.45/kW for applications on/after 6/1/2021; minimum customer & distribution charge $10.
grid_charging_allowed: No - customer-generator storage must be 'configured to receive electrical charge solely from an onsite renewable energy resource' (RSC and NMT)
standby_charge: NBC per nameplate kW (NMT rider NBC $0.45/kW for apps on/after 6/1/2021); NMT $10 minimum customer & distribution charge
storage_specific_notes: Battery retrofit on legacy/NMT: NMT dates are fixed by the 'original interconnection application date for the generation system, which may predate the current Customer's service', and Nameplate Capacity changes must be reported within 60 days - suggests a battery addition does not reset NMT dates, but not stated (Unclear). Battery must be renewable-charged only to stay on NMT/RSC. 20 kW AC cap covers 'installed generation system and equipment'.

rule_summary: Solar Choice rider to Residential Rate 5 (Order 2021-391, eff. 6/1/2021; revision E2026-138 eff. 7/1/2026 accepted, not read): TOU Rate 5 required; excess kWh netted within on-/off-peak period and banked month to month by period; bank cashed out at avoided cost (Rate PR-1 off-peak winter energy credit) in November billing; minimum bill $13.50; minimum term 10 years; customer keeps RECs; customer must furnish a meter socket for a separate generation meter measuring 100% of generator output; not combinable with PR-1 or Act 236 DER programs. Legacy 2015 NEM rider (closed 8/12/2015, terminated 12/31/2020) barred batteries entirely.
export_credit_value: kWh-for-kWh within same TOU period; unused November bank paid at PR-1 off-peak winter avoided energy credit (value not read)
grid_charging_allowed: No - rider definition limits storage to a device 'configured to receive electrical charge solely from an onsite Renewable Energy Resource'
standby_charge: Minimum bill $13.50/month
storage_specific_notes: Separate generation meter (customer-provided socket measuring 100% of generator output) is required - relevant to AC-coupled battery metering configuration (placement relative to battery not specified). Renewable-only charging required. Old 2015 net metering rider prohibited batteries outright; legacy (pre-6/1/2021) DESC NEM riders not reviewed for battery-retrofit treatment (Unclear). DESC also has a 'Rate PR - Storage' schedule (not read).

rule_summary: GA state row is built from Georgia Power's RNR-11 and Rules and Regs. Deviations from the statutory floor: commercial RNR up to 250 kW AC (100-250 kW <=125% prior-year peak); Energy Offset Only (EOO) non-export agreement as default; $100 residential / $200 C&I interconnection fee; mandatory system impact study and witness testing at >=250 kW with IEEE 1547-2018 communications interface. RNR-Monthly Netting pilot (5,000 customers) closed, sunsets no later than 12/31/2038. Customer-Sited Solar Plus Storage Pilot (2025 IRP) and PowerClerk BTM process per BTM Summary rev. 08.15.2025.
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 250 kW AC (100-250 kW <=125% of prior-year metered peak)
nem_aggregate_cap: 0.2% of prior-year annual peak demand (RNR-Instantaneous)
export_credit_value: Solar Avoided Energy Cost + 4 c/kWh Renewable Generation Adder (instantaneous netting)
ic_application_fee: $100 residential; $200 C&I (covers witness test <250 kW)
external_disconnect: Required - one-line must show generation AC disconnect(s) isolating the facility
non_export_option: Yes - Energy Offset Only (EOO) agreement; DB 18-23 non-exporting generator form for backup-capable storage
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - RNR-11 credits any metered Excess Energy with no rule on battery charging source; BTM summary describes batteries for self-consumption
storage_specific_notes: Battery inverter capacity counts: residential customer whose battery system has max inverter capability >10 kW (even if derated) cannot join RNR. Battery inverters/AC-coupled gateways must be UL 1741 SB + IEEE 1547-2018; backup operation requires open-transition, mechanically interlocked transfer switch and DB 18-23 non-export form. Adding a battery to a legacy RNR-Monthly Netting account: tariff silent (participation non-transferable between premises, 15-yr term) - Unclear whether allowed without losing monthly netting.

utility_name: Santee Cooper (South Carolina Public Service Authority)
rule_summary: State authority, not bound by Act 62 Solar Choice tariffs. Rider DG-25 (residential and non-residential; industrial variant up to 2,000 kW): hourly netting - within each hour, exports subtract from deliveries; net-negative hours credited at energy credit $0.0415/kWh (adjusted at least annually, no seasonality since April 2025 rates); net-positive hours billed at retail; residential DG customer charge $10/month; metering and standby fees eliminated April 2025; bill credit >= $50 paid by check, else carried forward. Interconnection under SCPSA Generator Interconnection Procedures (eff. 8/31/2016; 20 kW inverter process, fast track, study) and DG Standard; $100 residential application fee; liability insurance per Interconnection Standard.
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 1000 kW (and <= max monthly demand); industrial 2,000 kW
nem_aggregate_cap: None (former 2% of distribution class demand cap removed)
export_credit_value: $0.0415/kWh for hourly net exports (DG-25)
ic_application_fee: $100 residential
external_disconnect: Required - isolation device (manual load-break disconnect/safety switch) per Solar Home program manual
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - DG-25 applies to 'photovoltaic or other qualifying generation source' as determined by the Authority; silent on batteries and on charging source
standby_charge: Eliminated April 2025 (Authority may adjust for non-PV sources); $10/month residential DG customer charge
storage_specific_notes: DG-25 and 2016 interconnection procedures do not mention storage. Solar Home rebate covers PV portion only, not batteries. Because netting is hourly with export valued at 4.15 c/kWh, battery shifting of solar into same-hour load is the value lever. No legacy-NEM grandfathering to lose (already net billing since 2015).

rule_summary: Distribution co-op (not PSC rate-regulated). Renewable Surplus Rider for new installs: residential up to 20 kW AC and small commercial up to 100 kW AC (transformer <100 kVA), non-demand, non-time-of-day rates only; size also limited to annual kWh/1,800 (kW AC) or average monthly kWh/150 due to wholesale power agreement; exports credited at 6.03 c/kWh (updated about March 1 each year); $150 interconnection fee plus $50 per field inspection; homeowner's insurance declaration required; interconnection via breaker panel only (no meter-base connections); outdoor disconnect near meter; bi-directional meter. Larger accounts may self-consume with no value for surplus.
ic_application_fee: $150 + $50 per inspection
external_disconnect: Required (outdoor disconnect near meter, left open for co-op inspection)
non_export_option: Large accounts (>100 kVA) may install larger systems with no surplus compensation (de facto self-consumption)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - website and rider summary silent on batteries; interconnection standard PDF is a scanned image (not text-searchable)
storage_specific_notes: No storage provisions found. Not available with Time-of-Day rate, so TOU arbitrage plus export credit cannot be combined.

rule_summary: EMC; price and interconnection set by its board under O.C.G.A. 46-3-56(b),(d). Net Metering Rider (eff. 1/1/2022, applies to DG connected after 1/1/2016): solar PV, fuel cell or wind, <=10 kW residential / <=100 kW commercial (larger at co-op discretion), intended primarily to offset own use; $10/month incremental service cost; any generation exceeding consumption credited at avoided energy cost ($0.0432/kWh for 2026), credit balance carried to next bill and paid by check each December; Jackson EMC retains RECs; Distributed Generation Interconnection Agreement required; interconnection bulletin available on request, requests handled individually.
export_credit_value: $0.0432/kWh avoided energy cost (2026)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - Net Metering Rider silent on storage
standby_charge: $10/month incremental service cost
storage_specific_notes: No storage provisions in the rider; interconnection bulletin not public. Residential TOU rate has a Jan 1-May 1 enrollment window (program chunk).

rule_summary: EMC. Net Energy Metering Rider NEM-18 (eff. 5/1/2026) with Policy 412 and Small DG Interconnection Procedure (<=100 kW AC): solar PV, fuel cell or wind; generally <=10 kW AC residential / <=100 kW AC commercial; 0.2% of prior-year peak aggregate cap; Excess Net Energy settled monthly for DG interconnected on/before 1/1/2024 and instantaneously for DG interconnected on/after 1/2/2024; purchase rate for solar PV $0.0379/kWh all months (non-solar seasonal $0.0345-0.0398); co-op keeps RECs on purchased excess; no application fee for small DG; lockable visible-break disconnect near meter, separate one per source (solar and BESS) unless one isolates both; UL 1741 inverters (UL 1741 SA settings certified); applications valid 90 days.
nem_cap_res_kw: 10 kW AC (generation plus storage, unless BESS is non-export)
nem_aggregate_cap: 0.2% of prior-year annual peak demand
export_credit_value: $0.0379/kWh solar PV (NEM-18, eff. 5/1/2026)
ic_application_fee: $0 for Small DG (<=100 kW)
external_disconnect: Required - lockable visible-break switch near meter, one per energy source (solar, BESS) unless a single switch isolates both
non_export_option: Yes - BESS certified (PE or licensed electrician letter) as programmed to prevent export beyond the point of common coupling; co-op may also limit aggregate export capacity
grid_charging_allowed: Requires non-export - Small DG procedure requires a BESS to be programmed to prevent export beyond the PCC (exception: co-op-run BESS Program where the co-op dispatches the battery)
storage_specific_notes: Sizing: residential 'peak generating capacity and storage capacity' generally <=10 kW AC, but storage is excluded from the 10/100 kW threshold if a BESS control system prevents export. Battery exports are not creditable outside a co-op BESS Program. Grandfathering: monthly settlement applies to DG interconnected on/before 1/1/2024; whether adding a (non-export) battery to such a system triggers a new interconnection date and instantaneous settlement is not stated (Unclear).

rule_summary: EMC; board-set rules under O.C.G.A. 46-3-56. Schedule DG-1 (eff. 1/1/2026) applies to any Member Generator under the co-op's Distributed Generation Policy: DG capacity may not exceed the rated capacity of the co-op distribution equipment serving the member; member billed on its normal rate schedule plus a monthly facility charge 'when applicable'; excess net energy purchased at $0.04554/kWh (avoided average energy and capacity cost) for DG connected on/after 7/1/2015, and $0.0683/kWh 'until further notice' for DG connected before 7/1/2015; rates adjustable annually by the board. Interconnect agreement via online portal at least 45 days before interconnection; all interconnections at the breaker panel; $100 interconnection fee billed after net-meter swap. Solar members may take any rate except Even Bill.
nem_cap_res_kw: Not published (capped at rated capacity of serving distribution equipment)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: Not published (capped at rated capacity of serving distribution equipment)
export_credit_value: $0.04554/kWh for DG connected on/after 7/1/2015; $0.0683/kWh legacy (pre-7/1/2015) (DG-1 eff. 1/1/2026)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - DG-1 and solar pages silent on storage charging source; co-op battery page says battery energy 'can come from excess power produced by rooftop solar or from the grid' (general explainer only)
standby_charge: Monthly facility charge 'when applicable' (amount not published)
storage_specific_notes: No storage rules found in DG-1 or on the rooftop-solar pages; DG Policy document (defines Member Generator and DG Facility) not found online. Legacy grandfathering: pre-7/1/2015 DG keeps $0.0683/kWh 'until further notice' keyed to the date the facility connected - whether adding a battery (new interconnect agreement) moves a legacy system onto $0.04554 is not stated (Unclear). Netting interval (instantaneous vs billing-period) not stated; billing uses a bidirectional net meter.

rule_summary: EMC; board-set rules under O.C.G.A. 46-3-56. Schedule DG-2 Distributed Generation Service rider (effective billing rendered 10/1/2021; still the version linked from the rate-schedule page): applies to any member operating a DG Facility under the co-op's Distributed Generation Policy; written DG Interconnection Agreement required; bi-directional meter with two registers - for each billing period all energy delivered is billed at the member's regular retail rate and all energy received from the member is purchased at the Purchase Rate (i.e. instantaneous/two-channel netting, no kWh banking); purchase rate = estimated average annual avoided cost of energy, $0.02855/kWh as of the rider's effective date, adjustable at any time; optional monthly service charge = Facilities Charge (incremental facilities x Facilities Charge factor) plus administrative charge; purchase obligation first-come first-served up to 0.2% of prior-year annual peak demand. Interconnection: online residential application, contractor uploads site plan, one-line, inverter/panel specs 'and if applicable, back-up battery information'; engineering approval before install; signed electrical permit after install; wet-ink signatures on the agreement.
nem_aggregate_cap: 0.2% of prior-year annual peak demand (purchase obligation)
export_credit_value: $0.02855/kWh avoided energy cost (DG-2, eff. 10/1/2021; may since have been adjusted - not verified)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - DG-2 silent on storage and charging source; interconnection process only asks for 'back-up battery information' if applicable
standby_charge: Possible monthly Facilities Charge + administrative charge (amounts not published)
storage_specific_notes: Batteries are reviewed in the interconnection application (back-up battery information) but no storage-specific rules published. Because DG-2 already nets two-channel per billing period (all exports at avoided cost), there is no retail-rate legacy NEM to lose by adding a battery; whether a battery addition requires a new interconnection agreement is not stated (Unclear). Separate Cooperative Solar (community solar) rider exists. DG Policy document not found online.

rule_summary: EMC; board-set rules under O.C.G.A. 46-3-56 (Georgia Cogeneration and Distributed Generation Act of 2001). Member Generated Renewable Resource Rate Schedule (Cogen 2010): solar PV, fuel cell, hydro or wind, owned and operated by the member on its premises, intended to offset part or all of its requirements; peak generating capacity <=50 kW residential / <=100 kW commercial; customer-owner pays all interconnection costs and incremental metering cost (currently $800); each request handled individually. Bi-directional metering (behind the meter): retail tariff plus service charge for supplied energy, all kWh fed back credited at avoided energy cost each billing period; credit balance applied to next month's bill. Single-directional metering (utility side): all metered generation paid at avoided energy cost. Avoided energy cost $0.04247/kWh stated effective 7/1/2020 through 12/31/2025 (2026 value not published). Purchase obligation first-come first-served to 0.50% of prior-year annual peak demand; more at negotiated price.
nem_aggregate_cap: 0.50% of prior-year annual peak demand (purchase obligation; additional purchases negotiable)
export_credit_value: $0.04247/kWh avoided energy cost (stated effective 7/1/2020-12/31/2025; 2026 value not published)
ic_application_fee: $800 metering equipment and installation (plus all interconnection costs)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - rate schedule page silent on storage and charging source
standby_charge: Service charge per applicable tariff (amount not stated on DG page)
storage_specific_notes: No storage provisions found; eligible technologies listed are solar PV, fuel cell, hydro and wind only - a battery is not itself an eligible generator, and whether battery kW counts toward the 50/100 kW limit is not stated (Unclear). Exports are already credited at avoided cost per billing period (two-channel), so there is no legacy retail NEM to lose by adding a battery; retrofit treatment not stated.

rule_summary: EMC (NCUC-filed rate schedules, Docket EC-82 Sub 25; not subject to the Duke NMB/RSC order). Residential Net Metering Rider NM-R (eff. 4/1/2024): customer-side Renewable Generation (PV, fuel cell, micro-turbine, biomass, small wind; QF-eligible), customer must own the property; Option A (retail-rate kWh credit per billing month with $2.70/kW nameplate standby charge) CLOSED 4/1/2024; Option B (open since 7/1/2018): no standby charge, kWh delivered to the co-op credited at Rate Schedule AC avoided cost (two-channel billing, net monthly credit carried to next bill); switch options at most once a year on 60 days notice; customer keeps RECs; $100,000 homeowner liability insurance. Avoided cost (Schedule AC, eff. 2/1/2026) 5.058 c/kWh solar / 5.038 c/kWh non-solar, recalculated at least annually. Non-residential net metering is a pilot (NRNM). Small Generation Interconnection Standard (25 kW residential / 150 kW non-residential, single-phase): IEEE 1547 + UL 1741, lockable visible 'Generator Disconnect Switch', circuit saturation screens (30/60/100 kW per circuit by voltage), impact screens within 30 days, agreement within 10 days; application fee $250 residential / $500 non-residential (website; the 2019 standard PDF still says $100/$250). SGPPS 'sell all' rider to 20 kW residential / 100 kW non-residential.
nem_cap_res_kw: Lesser of estimated max annual demand or 10 kW (Options A/B); Option B up to 25 kW after 10/1/2020
nem_cap_nonres_kw: Individual basis above 100 kW (SGPPS); NRNM pilot limits not read
export_credit_value: 5.058 c/kWh solar / 5.038 c/kWh non-solar avoided cost (Schedule AC eff. 2/1/2026), Option B; legacy Option A = retail energy charge
ic_application_fee: $250 residential / $500 non-residential (non-refundable)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 25 (residential; 150 kW non-residential) - above Small Generation Standard scope
external_disconnect: Required - lockable visible-break 'Generator Disconnect Switch' near point of interconnection, accessible to co-op
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - NM-R and the Small Generation Standard are silent on storage and on charging source
standby_charge: Option A only: $2.70/kW nameplate per month (closed 4/1/2024); none for Option B
storage_specific_notes: No storage provisions in NM-R, Schedule AC or the 2019 Interconnection Standard. Battery retrofit: Standard 4.10 prohibits changes to Generator output capacity or protection system without a new Application and new acceptance - so adding a battery that changes output capacity requires re-application; whether a legacy Option A (retail-credit) customer can keep Option A after re-applying, when Option A is closed to new service, is not stated (Unclear). Option B already credits exports at avoided cost, so little legacy value is at stake there.

rule_summary: Follows SC state row (Act 62). DEP SC: Rider RSC (SC Second Revised Leaf 663, eff. 1/1/2026, Order 2021-390) requires Schedule R-STOU; per-TOU-period netting within the month, CPP-hour exports netted against On-Peak; Monthly Credit for Net Excess Energy $0.0401/kWh; non-bypassable charge on Nameplate kW DC (solar) / kW AC (non-solar) (amount not stated in rider); minimum bill = Basic Facilities Charge plus schedule minimums, excess credits applied after minimum bill; 1-yr minimum term; 100% power factor. Rider NMT (SC Original Leaf 671, eff. 1/1/2026, Order 2025-453) for legacy Rider RNM / IRSC customers: any residential rate, monthly netting with TOU-period ordering, Net Excess Energy Credit 4.01 c/kWh; up to 10 years from NMT Start Date (1/1/2026 for original interconnection applications before 5/16/2019, ending 12/31/2035; 6/1/2029 for applications on/after 5/16/2019, ending 5/31/2039), then Rider RSC; enrollment window 6 months before to 12 months after NMT Start. NMT NBC: base $0.00/kW; rider NBC $0.47/kW for applications on/after 6/1/2021; IRSC customers also pay NBC for non-service volumetric riders; minimum customer & distribution charge $10.
export_credit_value: RSC $0.0401/kWh; NMT 4.01 c/kWh (both eff. 1/1/2026)
grid_charging_allowed: No - RSC and NMT Customer-Generator definition admits only 'an energy storage device configured to receive electrical charge solely from an onsite renewable energy resource'
standby_charge: RSC NBC per nameplate kW (amount in R-STOU, not read); NMT rider NBC $0.47/kW (apps on/after 6/1/2021); NMT $10 minimum customer & distribution charge
storage_specific_notes: Same structure as DEC SC. Battery retrofit on legacy RNM/NMT: NMT dates and NBC tiers are fixed by the 'original interconnection application date for the generation system, which may predate the current Customer's service', and Nameplate Capacity changes must be reported within 60 days - suggests a battery addition does not reset NMT dates, but not stated (Unclear). Battery must be renewable-charged only to remain a Customer-Generator. 20 kW AC cap covers 'installed generation system and equipment' (whether battery inverter kW counts: Unclear). DEP SC also has a Non-Residential Storage Demand Response tariff (eff. 3/1/2026, not read).

rule_summary: Follows FPSC Rule 25-6.065 tiers (T1 <=10 kW, T2 <=100 kW, T3 <=2 MW AC; AC = DC x 0.85). Adds a sizing screen not in the rule: system must be estimated to produce <115% of annual kWh consumption; NEM systems >=50 kW must interconnect three-phase wye. Tier 2 fee $400, Tier 3 fee $1,000; Tier 2 insurance $1M. FPL requires a lockable visible-break manual disconnect for Tier 2 and Tier 3 (waived for inverter-based Tier 1 per rule).
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $400; Tier 3 $1,000 (plus study charge if required)
external_disconnect: Required for Tier 2 and Tier 3 (adjacent to meter, lockable); waived Tier 1
non_export_option: Yes for stand-alone batteries: grid-charged storage without renewables submits a Small Generator Interconnection Application; if non-exporting and no utility equipment needed, no interconnection agreement is required
storage_specific_notes: FPL battery policy: battery paired with NEM renewable system is for customer use only and may NOT export to the grid (so battery energy never earns NEM credit); UL 1741 certification required, non-UL batteries must be DC-coupled behind a UL 1741 device; meter placard 'Battery storage utilized in this facility'. Tier 3 batteries reviewed in fast-track study. Stand-alone storage is not 'renewable' under 25-6.065(2)(d) and its output is not net metered. Adding a battery to an existing NEM system: no loss of NEM status stated (FL has no legacy/successor split); interconnection agreement sec. 7 requires a new application/agreement 30 days ahead only if gross power rating increases -- whether an AC-coupled battery counts as a rating increase is Unclear. Policy stated as subject to change.

rule_summary: No AL statewide NEM/interconnection rule; Alabama Power tariffs are the rule (see AL state row). No net metering: exports bought under Rate PAE (<=100 kW) at avoided cost (~4.4-7.7c/kWh by TOU period); Rate Rider RGB capacity reservation charge $5.41/kW-month (secondary) on generator nameplate or RTA 71c/kWh summer 3-5pm alternative. 3-tier DER process: Tier I <=25 kW $0, Tier II <=100 kW $500, Tier III >100 kW $1,000 screen. IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB; lockable visible-break AC disconnect required.
export_credit_value: Rate PAE TOD option: Jun-Sep 7.44c/kWh (wkdy 10am-9pm CT) / 5.23c; Oct-May 4.86c / 4.41c (rev. eff. April 2023 billings as posted)
ic_application_fee: Tier I $0; Tier II $500; Tier III $1,000 screening (+$10k-$50k if studies)
external_disconnect: Required (manual, visible-break, lockable, 24/7 accessible)
non_export_option: Yes: Non-Export / Limited-Export Generation defined in DER TIR Guidebook; UL 1741 CRD PCS or UL 3141 power control systems accepted; RGB still applies to non-exporting generation
standby_charge: Rate Rider RGB Capacity Reservation Charge $5.41/kW-month secondary, $4.87/kW-month primary, on nameplate of on-site non-emergency generation; upheld by M.D. Ala. 2026-03-25 (appeal status unverified)
standby_threshold_kw: None (applies to all parallel non-emergency generation)
storage_specific_notes: Storage is a DER under the APC Guidebook (spec sheets must give battery kW, kWh). Adding a battery to an existing PV system is a modification: any addition/removal or inverter change requires a NEW interconnection application and permission to operate before paralleling; SLD must show battery as new and PV as existing. No NEM grandfathering exists to lose, but whether a battery (esp. grid-charged or non-exporting) adds to RGB-billed nameplate kW is Unclear. PAE purchases only energy from a PURPA qualifying facility, so export of grid-charged battery energy under PAE is Unclear/likely not credited. V2G/V2H: normal application, external disconnect and MID required.

rule_summary: Follows FPSC Rule 25-6.065 tiers (T1 <=10 kW, T2 >10-100 kW, T3 >100 kW-2 MW) under Net Metering Rider; utility-set fees: Tier 1 $0, Tier 2 $240, Tier 3 $750 (+ study; results within 60 days). Insurance T1 recommended $100k (not required), T2 $1M, T3 $2M. Tier 2/3 require externally accessible lockable manual AC load-break disconnect (not a breaker) near meter. Service-drop screen: PV rating <=90% of transformer/service rating or customer pays upgrade. Tier 1 PTO usually within 10 business days of completion.
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $240; Tier 3 $750
external_disconnect: Required Tier 2 and Tier 3 (visible-break, lockable, labeled Generator Disconnect Switch); not required Tier 1
storage_specific_notes: DEF net-metering tier pages and application do not address batteries (unlike FPL, no published battery-export prohibition found). Whether battery export earns NEM credit, whether grid charging is permitted on a NEM account, and whether adding a battery to an existing NEM system requires a new application: all Unclear from DEF published material. No legacy/successor NEM split in FL, so no grandfathering to lose. DEF runs EnergyWise Home Battery Control DR (see programs).

rule_summary: Follows FPSC Rule 25-6.065 via Rate Schedule NM-1 and Standard Interconnection Agreements (Tier 1 <=10 kW, Tier 2 >10-100 kW, Tier 3 >100 kW-2 MW AC; GPR = DC x 0.85; GPR <=90% of service rating). Utility-set fees: Tier 2 $250 one-time (no charge for any Tier 2 study); Tier 3 $500 + study deposit $3,000 (actual cost, capped $3,000). Insurance T2 $1M, T3 $2M (self-insurance by approval). Visible load-break lockable manual disconnect adjacent to meter required T2/T3. Agreement executed within 30 days (90 if Tier 3 study); PTO notice within 10 business days. Agreements still cite IEEE 1547-2003/UL 1741-2005.
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $250; Tier 3 $500 + study up to $3,000 (deposit $3,000)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 100 (Tier 3; Tier 2 study at no charge if needed)
external_disconnect: Required Tier 2 and Tier 3 (visible load-break, lockable, exterior adjacent to meter)
storage_specific_notes: Agreements define RGS as renewable generation only; batteries not addressed in NM-1 agreements read. TECO Steps to Connect page reportedly states batteries are interconnected but not net metered (search-snippet only; page could not be loaded, redirect loop) -- implies battery discharge does not earn NEM credit: Unverified. Adding a battery: agreement sec. 7 requires a new application 30 days ahead only for a change in GPR; whether a battery changes GPR is Unclear. No legacy NEM tier to lose in FL.

rule_summary: Municipal; exempt from FPSC Rule 25-6.065 (s. 366.91(6) F.S. requires own program). JEA Distributed Generation Policy eff. 2018-04-01 replaced net metering: monthly netting but exported kWh credited at JEA fuel rate (~3c/kWh at launch) instead of retail; credits accrue through calendar year and remaining balance paid at year end per policy. Systems passing final inspection by 2018-03-31 grandfathered under retired Net Metering Policy (Tiers 1-3, full retail) for 20 years; 10 MW aggregate cap applied to legacy Tier 1-3 net metering. Interconnection via PowerClerk; JEA DER Technical Interconnection & Interoperability Requirements (2025).
nem_aggregate_cap: 10 MW aggregate for legacy Tier 1-3 net metering (closed 2018)
export_credit_value: Exports credited at JEA fuel charge rate (post-2018-04-01 systems); legacy NM systems full retail through 20-yr grandfather
external_disconnect: Required (utility disconnect); separate battery load disconnect if permanently mounted battery(ies) (per JEA DER requirements, search snippet)
storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to a legacy (pre-4/1/2018) net-metered system: JEA pages state (per search snippet) that a grandfathered NM customer who takes JEA Battery Incentive loses grandfathering and moves to the Distributed Generation (fuel-rate) program -- the retrofit trigger is taking the incentive; whether a self-funded battery retrofit also forfeits grandfathering is Unclear. JEA itself framed batteries as a way to self-consume rather than export at fuel rate (2018 rebate up to $4,000, first 50). jea.com blocks automated fetch (CAPTCHA) so policy text not read directly.

rule_summary: Municipal; own TruNet Solar net metering program (s. 366.91(6) F.S.). Tiers by AC gross power rating mirror FPSC tiers: Tier 1 0-10 kW no fee; Tier 2 >10-100 kW $340; Tier 3 >100 kW-2 MW $1,300. Systems connected/approved by 2025-06-30 grandfathered at full retail through 2045-06-30. Systems interconnected after 2025-06-30: full retail during grace period through 2026-10-31, then Community Solar Energy rate through 2030-06-30, then Retail Levelized Fuel rate. From 2026-11-01 exports credited within the same billing period (no kWh rollover); leftover $ credit carries forward on account. Annual true-up done Dec 2025 plus a final true-up Fall 2026. Sizing: capacity should not exceed home energy needs. MID-TRANSITION: successor rates take effect Nov 2026.
export_credit_value: Legacy (<=2025-06-30): full retail ~10.7c/kWh residential through 2045; new: full retail to 2026-10-31, then Community Solar Energy rate (~4.6c/kWh per program chunk, Secondary) to 2030-06-30, then Retail Levelized Fuel rate
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $340; Tier 3 $1,300
storage_specific_notes: Battery retrofit on legacy system: taking OUC Battery Storage Rebate requires forfeiting TruNet Full Retail Rate (10.7c/kWh) on all exports -- i.e., a rebated battery retrofit loses grandfathering. An add-on PV array does NOT affect grandfathered status (OUC FAQ); whether a self-funded (non-rebate) battery retrofit affects grandfathering is not stated: Unclear. Applications may be solar or solar+battery. Grid-charging rules not published.

rule_summary: Co-op; own Net Metering Rider (Sheet 11.000, eff. 2023-02-01) modeled on FPSC Rule 25-6.065 but with deviations: Tier 3 capped at 1 MW (not 2 MW); net-metered customers billed on a separate flat (non-tiered) Net Metering rate (RS 8.21c/kWh total energy + $22.22 customer charge vs. standard inverted-block rate). Monthly kWh netting; excess kWh carried forward to end of calendar year and paid at LCEC calculated avoided purchased power cost for prior year. Fees: Tier 1 $35 (rule has $0 for IOUs), Tier 2 up to $1,000, Tier 3 $1,000 (+ study up to $2,000 per LCEC fees page). Tier 2 insurance $1M; lockable visible load-break disconnect within 5 ft of meter (Tier 2). GPR <=90% of service/transformer rating. Standby or resale service not permitted under rider.
nem_cap_res_kw: 1000 (Tier 3 max; rule applies 1 MW, not 2 MW)
export_credit_value: 1:1 kWh netting at Net Metering Rider flat rate (RS 8.21c/kWh energy + PCA); year-end excess paid at LCEC avoided purchased power cost (prior year)
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $35; Tier 2 up to $1,000; Tier 3 $1,000 (+ study fee up to $2,000 if applicable)
external_disconnect: Required Tier 2 (visible load-break, lockable, within 5 ft of meter); Tier 1 not verified
standby_charge: Standby service not permitted under Net Metering Rider
storage_specific_notes: Rider and agreements cover renewable generation systems only; batteries not addressed. Agreement requires a new application 30 days before modifications that increase GPR; whether a battery increases GPR is Unclear. No legacy/successor split at LCEC so no grandfathering to lose. Grid charging/battery export credit: Unclear.

rule_summary: Co-op; own Net Metering Rider and single-form "Interconnection and Parallel Operation of Renewable Distribution Generation" agreement (rev. 10/22/19) instead of FPSC 25-6.065 tiered agreements. Net meter measures delivered and received kWh; excess over the year purchased at year end at the avoided cost of wholesale supplier Seminole Electric Cooperative. Agreement: 1-yr auto-renewing term; co-op may terminate service at its sole discretion or disconnect without notice for safety; access required for WREC and Seminole; no intentional islanding (IEEE 1547). Tier sizes, fees and insurance not stated in agreement; Net Metering Rider text not read.
export_credit_value: Monthly netting (retail); annual excess paid at Seminole Electric avoided cost
storage_specific_notes: WREC solar FAQ treats batteries only as storing excess PV for self-use (battery-backed systems); no statement on battery export credit, grid charging, or retrofit treatment. No legacy/successor split so no grandfathering to lose. Unclear on all storage-specific rules.

rule_summary: Co-op (Sumter Electric Cooperative d/b/a SECO Energy); own Net Metering tariff Sheet 16.4 + Interconnection Agreement Sheets 17.0-17.5 (eff. 2022-04-01) under Seminole Electric wholesale contract. Tiers per 25-6.065 but capped at 1,000 kW AC (not 2 MW); GPR (DC x 0.85) <=90% of service rating. Net billing, not retail NEM: all kWh taken from grid billed at otherwise applicable rate; excess kWh delivered to grid in each billing cycle credited at base cost of power (Schedule PCA) + monthly WPCA factor (wholesale/avoided cost). Credits only to the service behind which system sits. Insurance: none <=10 kW, $1M >10 kW (co-op as additional insured). Lockable manual disconnect separate from meter socket required for all sizes. IEEE 1547 / UL 1741 latest version. AMI bi-directional meter required. PTO within 10 business days.
export_credit_value: Excess kWh each billing cycle credited at Schedule PCA base cost of power + WPCA factor (wholesale power cost), not retail
external_disconnect: Required all tiers (lockable manual disconnect, separate from meter socket, readily accessible)
storage_specific_notes: SECO interconnection agreement explicitly lists "battery storage" among RGS energy sources (rare in FL) -- battery may interconnect under the standard agreement. Because exports are credited at wholesale cost of power in the same billing cycle (net billing), battery self-consumption shifting has value; whether grid-charged battery exports are credited is not addressed: Unclear. Adding a battery: new application required 30 days ahead for any GPR change; whether battery kW counts toward GPR/1 MW cap is Unclear. No legacy tier to lose.

rule_summary: Co-op (Seminole Electric member); own Form IGRG-1 Interconnection Agreement (Sheets 21.0-21.04, eff. 2026-04-30) and "Avoided Cost" net billing program. RGS rated <=1,000 kW AC and should be designed not to exceed member service load consumption; >=20 kW requires engineering pre-approval; GPR (DC x 0.85) <=90% of service entrance rating or co-op transformer kVA, and co-op will not upsize distribution equipment for oversized RGS. Export: excess kWh bought back at current Seminole QF-1 wholesale rate and credited on next bill (not retail). Insurance: $100k for <=10 kW (stricter than FPSC rule), $1M >10 kW. Lockable manual disconnect separate from meter socket required for all sizes. Net meter install $60 trip fee; processing fee at co-op discretion.
nem_cap_res_kw: 1000 (agreement max; sized to load; >=20 kW pre-approval)
export_credit_value: Excess kWh credited at Seminole QF-1 wholesale (avoided cost) rate
ic_application_fee: Processing fee at co-op discretion (not stated); $60 net-meter trip fee
external_disconnect: Required all sizes (lockable manual disconnect, outside, accessible, separate from meter socket)
non_export_option: Stand-alone batteries (no RGS) may only charge from grid and may not interconnect/parallel; UL-listed automatic transfer switch required
storage_specific_notes: Agreement sec. 12 (2026): battery paired with RGS must be UL 1741 certified with meter placard "Battery storage utilized in this facility"; battery is solely for customer use and shall NOT export to the co-op; backup operation only when isolated (UL ATS or special inverter). Batteries are not renewable under Rule 25-6.065(2)(d); battery-only systems may charge from grid but may not interconnect (ATS required). So battery discharge never earns QF-1 credit and grid arbitrage via export is prohibited. Adding a battery is permitted under these guidelines; exceeding approved battery capacity is a disconnection ground, implying battery must be declared (new application for GPR changes 30 days ahead). No legacy retail NEM to lose.

rule_summary: Municipal (City of Lakeland); own Net Metering Service schedule Sheets 8.4-8.6 (eff. 2023-10-01). PV only (static inverters). Tiers: T1 <=10 kW, T2 <=100 kW (residential), T3 <=2 MW (commercial). Sizing: PV may not exceed 100% of annual consumption; >90% of transformer/service capacity at customer expense. Exports metered on separate register and credited at full retail; kWh credits carry forward on a moving 12-month window and expire unpaid at end of window (no annual cash-out); on termination accumulated credit paid at full retail.
